tiers.policy: Two tiers, no deletions. 'routing' skills are listed to Claude with their full description and may be invoked automatically. Every other skill is 'catalog' tier: it carries disable-model-invocation:true, so it costs no context, but stays installed, stays runnable as /claude-foundation:<name>, and stays discoverable via the generated skills/skill-index/CATALOG.md. Move a skill between tiers by editing the routing list below, then run: python3 scripts/generate_skill_index.py --apply. This is orthogonal to native Claude Code skill invocation: disable-model-invocation:true only controls whether Claude Code itself may resident-list or model-invoke a skill. It does not govern our own custom skill-bank-router/skill-index catalog-discovery mechanism, which is a separate routing_disposition axis (see manual_only below) deciding whether the router may load/apply a catalog-tier skill's guidance automatically from a matched prompt, versus requiring explicit user invocation.
tiers.manual_only_policy: routing_disposition default: every catalog-tier skill (any active skill not in tiers.routing) is CATALOG_AUTO by default -- skill-bank-router/skill-index may discover it via CATALOG.md and load/apply its SKILL.md as router-selected guidance for a matching prompt, without native Claude Code auto-invocation (still gated by disable-model-invocation:true). List a skill in tiers.manual_only to mark it MANUAL_ONLY: skill-bank-router/skill-index must NOT auto-apply it -- they must tell the user the explicit action/invocation required instead. Reserve MANUAL_ONLY for destructive, shared-state, production, release, deployment, secret-rotation, or other irreversible/high-blast-radius workflows. A skill cannot be both tiers.routing and tiers.manual_only (a routing-tier skill is already natively resident and auto-invocable, so 'manual only' would contradict its own tier) -- enforced by scripts/check_manifest_consistency.py --check.
